text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midianites. After that you will be gathered to your people."
So Moses said to the people, "Arm some of your men for war, so they can go against Midian and carry out the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
Send a thousand men to war from each of the tribes of Israel."
So from the clans of Israel a thousand were enlisted from each tribe—twelve thousand men armed for war.

versions.text: So a thousand from each tribe were handed over from the divisions of Israel—twelve thousand men armed for war.
versions.explanation: "handed over from the divisions" is stilted and the double prepositional phrase is hard to follow aloud; אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל refers to Israel's clans or family units, and "enlisted" fits the muster context.

text: Moses sent them out to war, a thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
Among the slain were the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the five kings of Midian. They also put Balaam son of Beor to the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian and their children captive, and they plundered all their herds, all their flocks, and all their goods.
They burned all the towns where the Midianites had settled, along with all their encampments.
They carried off all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and livestock,
and brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the assembly of the Israelites at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly went out to meet them outside the camp.
But Moses was angry with the officers of the army—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—who were returning from the campaign.
"Have you let all the women live?" he said to them.
"These were the very ones who followed Balaam's advice and enticed the Israelites to be unfaithful to the LORD in the affair at Peor, so that a plague struck the LORD's assembly.
Now kill every male among the children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep alive for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man.
As for you, stay outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed a person or touched a dead body must purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.

versions.text: As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed a person or touched a dead body must purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
versions.explanation: "camp outside the camp" repeats the same word awkwardly and stumbles when read aloud; "stay outside the camp" conveys the same sense of encamping while reading smoothly.

text: Purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything woven of goat hair, and every wooden object."
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the requirement of the law that the LORD gave Moses:
the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead—

anything that can withstand fire you must put through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must also be purified with the water of cleansing. And whatever cannot withstand fire you must pass through the water.
On the seventh day wash your clothes, and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp."
The LORD said to Moses,
"You, Eleazar the priest, and the family heads of the assembly are to count all that was captured, both people and livestock.
Divide the plunder between the fighting men who went into battle and the rest of the assembly.
From the soldiers who went into battle, set apart as a tribute for the LORD one out of every five hundred—of the people, the cattle, the donkeys, and the sheep and goats.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's portion.

From the Israelites' half, take one out of every fifty—of the people, the cattle, the donkeys, the sheep and goats, all the livestock—and give them to the Levites, who are charged with the care of the LORD's tabernacle."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The plunder remaining from the spoil taken by the fighting men was 675,000 sheep and goats,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 women who had never slept with a man.
The half belonging to those who had gone to war came to 337,500 sheep and goats,
of which the tribute for the LORD was 675;
36,000 cattle, of which the tribute for the LORD was 72;
30,500 donkeys, of which the tribute for the LORD was 61;
and 16,000 people, of whom the tribute for the LORD was 32.
Moses gave the tribute, the LORD's portion, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded him.
Then there was the Israelites' half, which Moses had divided off from the share of the fighting men:

versions.text: The Israelites' half, which Moses set apart from what belonged to the fighting men,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb חָצָה means "divided," and as it stands the English clause dangles without a predicate, leaving verses 42–43 grammatically tangled when read aloud. A clearer introduction sets up the list that follows.

text: The assembly's half came to 337,500 sheep and goats,

versions.text: the assembly's half, came to 337,500 sheep and goats,
versions.explanation: The comma after "half" wrongly separates subject from verb, and the lowercase opening depends on the incomplete sentence in verse 42. Beginning a fresh sentence makes the count clear for oral reading.

text: 36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.

From the Israelites' half Moses took one out of every fifty, both of the people and of the livestock, and gave them to the Levites, who were charged with the care of the LORD's tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

versions.text: From the Israelites' half Moses took one out of every fifty, both of the people and of the livestock, and gave them to the Levites, who were charged with the care of the LORD's tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew names Moses explicitly in the closing formula. Since the sentence is long and several other referents intervene (the Levites, the LORD), restoring the proper name removes any ambiguity for a listener.

text: Then the officers over the units of the army—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—came to Moses
and said to him, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one man is missing.
So we have brought as an offering to the LORD the gold articles each of us found—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants—to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the crafted articles.
All the gold that the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds presented to the LORD came to sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.

versions.text: All the gold from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds that they presented to the LORD weighed 16,750 shekels.
versions.explanation: The current wording separates 'gold from the commanders' from 'that they presented,' which is hard to follow when heard aloud. Spelling out the figure also reads more smoothly for oral delivery than a numeral.

text: Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
